dossier.name: Michael Abrams
dossier.role: EVP, Strategic Initiatives (per Crunchbase). Earlier he was President, Digital Ventures at Live Nation, and before that Senior Vice President of Innovation at The Walt Disney Company.
dossier.thesis: Not a traditional venture investor. Public records describe a Live Nation executive who ran the Live Nation Labs Fund, which made strategic investments in early-stage entertainment technology, but I found no current investment thesis.

brief.headline: Michael Abrams is a strategic rather than traditional venture contact, and his past work running the Live Nation Labs Fund in early-stage entertainment technology makes a live-events app that extends a concert ticket into a night out a plausible fit, though his current activity is unconfirmed.
brief.angle: Frame the startup as an add-on to the live-event experience that drives spend and engagement around ticketed shows, not as a standard venture bet on growth metrics. Confirm whether the Labs Fund or a similar strategic program is still active before leaning on this framing.
deck: Show how the app turns one ticket purchase into several follow-on purchases (bars, merch, rides) for the same night, with clear per-show numbers.
Explain the fanbase-specific picks in plain terms and show one example where a fanbase segment responded differently.
Position the comparables (Ticketmaster, Spotify, Uber) by what each one does for the user, not as valuation benchmarks.
Include a slide on how the app would work with event organizers and venues, since a strategic investor will ask about partnership fit.
avoid: Do not assume a current investment thesis; none was found, so ask what they are looking for now before pitching.
Do not present the deal as a conventional venture round with growth-stage metrics unless they ask for it.
Do not imply any personal affinity for a particular artist, brand or venue, since no public interests were found.
questions: Is the Live Nation Labs Fund or a similar strategic program still making investments, and what stage does it target?
How would a startup like this fit with existing ticketing and venue relationships, and would that create conflicts or advantages?
What evidence do you have that fans will spend beyond the ticket on a night out, and how repeatable is that per show?

picks.line: I noticed you backed Socialcam, and we're applying a similar bet on how mobile apps change social behavior, except around the live concert night out.

openers.line: You ran the Live Nation Labs Fund, so you've seen many ideas for the show itself. We think the bigger opportunity is the hours before and after the doors open.
Fans already use Ticketmaster, Spotify, and Uber for their concert plans. We built the layer that ties those together into one night out, chosen for each fanbase.
